newsitem.title: GERMANY: Victoria chief sees ERGO with 14 mln customers.
newsitem.headline: Victoria chief sees ERGO with 14 mln customers.

text.p: The chief executive of Victoria Holding AG Edgar Jannott said his company's merger with Hamburg-Mannheimer would create a mega-insurance company with more than 14 million customers.

Jannott, addressing Victoria's shareholder meeting, said the new company would lead the field in health and legal costs insurance and expected annual administrative cost savings of more than 150 million marks a year due to synergy effects.

Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG late on Thursday announced plans to merge Hamburg-Mannheimer and its DKV health insurer with Victoria to create Germany's second largest primary insurer after Allianz AG.

Based in Duesseldorf, the new ERGO Versicherungsgruppe will have total premium income of 21 billion marks, investments exceeding 100 billion marks, and annual profit of 380 million marks based on combined 1996 results.
The group will employ some 40,000 staff, Jannott said. It was too early to predict if jobs would be shed.
